sentences.text: This bail application is filed under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS').

2. Petitioner is the 3rd accused in Crime No.504/2025 of Varapuzha Police Station, Ernakulam,
registered alleging offences punishable under Sections 406 and 420 r/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
3. The prosecution case is that the accused, who is conducting an establishment by name M/s.Safe Chit Fund', had promised to provide a huge profit on the amount invested in the chit scheme of the establishment and believing the words of the accused, the defacto complainant paid an amount of Rs.3,000/- every month from 25.02.2010 to 27.02.2020 thereby investing a total amount of Rs.3,63,000/-, and thereafter, the accused failed to pay the interest or return the amount and thus committed the offences alleged.
4. I have heard the learned counsel for the petitioner as well as the learned Public Prosecutor.

5. The first accused in the same crime had approached the Sessions Court, Ernakulam seeking anticipatory bail and by order dated 30.06.2025 in BAIL APPL. NO. 9078 OF 2025 2025:KER:59701 Crl.M.C.No.1748/2025 he was granted anticipatory bail, since the defacto complainant appeared in person and submitted that the matter had been settled between the parties and an affidavit to that effect has been filed.
6.

The nature of allegations against the petitioner indicates that the main allegation was against the first accused and since the dispute between the first accused and the defacto complainant has been Tomy T T vs State Of Kerala on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2752946/
2 settled; the basis of the allegations against the petitioner is also effectively covered by the said settlement.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In such circumstances, I am satisfied that the petitioner need not be subjected to any custodial interrogation.

7. In Sushila Aggarwal and Others v. State (NCT of Delhi) and Another, [2020 (5) SCC 1], it was held that while considering whether to grant anticipatory bail or not, Courts ought to be generally guided by considerations such as the nature and gravity of the offences, the role attributed to the applicant,
and the facts of the case.

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal and Others v. State (NCT of Delhi) and Another, [2020 (5) SCC 1]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Grant of anticipatory bail is a matter of discretion and the kind of conditions to be imposed or not to be imposed are all dependent on facts of each case, and subject to the discretion of the court.

8. In Ashok Kumar v. State of Union Territory Chandigarh [2024 SCC OnLine SC 274], wherein it has been held that a mere assertion on the part of the State while opposing the plea for anticipatory bail that custodial interrogation is required would not be sufficient and that the State would have to show or indicate more than prima facie case as to why custodial interrogation of the accused is required for the purpose of investigation.

entities.text: Ashok Kumar v. State of Union Territory Chandigarh [2024 SCC OnLine SC 274]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, the State has not been able to convince BAIL APPL. NO. 9078 OF 2025 2025:KER:59701 this Court that custodial interrogation is necessary.
9. On a consideration of the circumstances arising in the case, this Court is of the view that though the allegations are serious in nature, custodial interrogation of the petitioner is not required.
Further, having regard to the nature of the offences and the severity of punishment, this Court is of the view that petitioner is entitled to be released on pre-arrest bail.

10. Accordingly, this application is allowed on the following conditions:
(a) In the event of the petitioner being arrested in Crime No.504/2025 of Varapuzha Police Station, he shall be released on bail on him executing a bond for Rs.50,000/-
(Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum before the Investigating Officer.
(b) Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer for interrogation if he is so required in writing and shall co-operate with the investigation.
(c) Petitioner shall not destroy or tamper with the evidence or intimidate or threaten or contact the defacto complainant or his family members.
(d) Petitioner shall not commit any other similar offences while he is on bail.
(e) Petitioner shall not leave India without the permission of the Court having jurisdiction.
BAIL APPL. NO. 9078 OF 2025 2025:KER:59701

In case of violation of any of the above conditions,
or if any modification or deletion of the conditions are required, the jurisdictional Court shall be Tomy T T vs State Of Kerala on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2752946/
3 empowered to consider such applications, if any, and pass appropriate orders in accordance with law, notwithstanding the bail having been granted by this Court.
